name: Muškat momjanski

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Sémillon, Cabernet Franc, Tempranillo, Dolcetto and Merlot fully without cooking off their freshness.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Marl is a limy clay. It holds water and makes vines ripen later, which keeps acidity in the grapes. Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil stores water through dry spells, but stays wet and cold after rain, which slows ripening and can swell the grapes. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
